summary: ansible_pwsh_interpreter chooses the PowerShell executable for modules. Windows allows absolute or relative paths while Linux/macOS require absolute paths, and by default Windows uses powershell.exe 5.1 for #!powershell modules and pwsh for #!/usr/bin/pwsh, while Linux/macOS always use /usr/bin/pwsh.
questions: How do I tell Ansible which PowerShell executable to use?
Can I use a relative path for pwsh on Linux?
Which PowerShell does Ansible use by default on Windows?
What is the default PowerShell interpreter on Linux targets?

answer_card.title: Configuring ansible_pwsh_interpreter
answer_card.answer_md:
`ansible_pwsh_interpreter` sets which PowerShell executable runs PowerShell modules.

**Paths:**
- Windows: absolute (`C:\Program Files\PowerShell\7\pwsh.exe`) or a name/relative path (`pwsh`, found via PATH)
- Linux/macOS: absolute paths only (`/usr/bin/pwsh`, `/opt/microsoft/powershell/7/pwsh`)

**Defaults (when not set):**
- Windows: `#!powershell` modules use `C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe` (5.1); `#!/usr/bin/pwsh` modules use `pwsh` (7)
- Linux/macOS: all modules use `/usr/bin/pwsh`

It can be set per play or task.
